name: MARS-Bench
intro: MARS-Bench 是首个面向火星科学任务的标准化评测基准，覆盖轨道和地表影像上的分类、分割与目标检测任务，用于系统评估基础模型在火星地质与遥感场景中的表现。
org: Arizona State University, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology
intro_en: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used in real-world conversational applications, but their robustness in handling long and complex dialogue sessions—including frequent shifts in intent and complex cross-turn dependencies—has been criticized. MARS-Bench is a multi-turn competitive real-world scenario dialogue benchmark designed to address this gap. It is constructed through detailed textual annotations per session and aims to evaluate three key aspects of multi-turn dialogue: ultra-long turns, interactive multi-turns, and cross-turn tasks.
flowchart_en:
flowchart LR
    A["Curate existing Mars science datasets from orbital and surface imagery sources"] --> B["Organize 20 datasets across classification, segmentation, and object detection tasks"]
    B --> C["Correct annotations with expert planetary-science validation and original-author review where available"]
    C --> D["Standardize data and annotations into machine-learning-ready formats including COCO, Pascal VOC, and YOLO"]
    D --> E["Create train, validation, test, few-shot, and domain partitions while preserving original splits where possible"]
    E --> F["Run natural-image, Earth-observation, and vision-language baselines under scratch, frozen, and fine-tuning settings"]
    F --> G["Repeat selected experiments with seven random seeds and validation-based hyperparameter selection"]
    G --> H["Report classification F1, segmentation IoU, detection mAP, IQM, and confidence intervals"]

drawio_review_note:
Aligned with arXiv:2510.24010. The paper describes Mars-Bench as 20 Mars science datasets spanning classification, segmentation, and object detection over orbital and surface imagery; created by curating, organizing, restructuring, and correcting existing datasets with expert validation; standardized into train/validation/test splits and COCO/Pascal VOC/YOLO-ready detection annotations; and evaluated with classification, segmentation, and detection baselines over seven random seeds using F1, IoU, mAP, IQM, and confidence intervals.

Bilingual Draw.io bundle synchronized from benchmark_importer after paper and official-source review. The Chinese and English specs use identical node IDs, semantic types, coordinates, edges, and waypoints; strict Draw.io validation, XML and link checks, and rendered-image visual review passed before publication.
